objective: Align the production Dockerfile with the declared Node >=22 engine and stop the keepalive workflow from labelling an HTTP 200 with application status degraded/offline as healthy. This change improves runtime consistency and operational truth; it does not certify production render acceptance.

okf.notes: This is a bounded operational follow-up to live evidence of an HTTP-200 but degraded readiness response. The full repository-wide .okf sweep and production-helper security tools were not executed through this GitHub-only session; disposition remains BLOCKED until repository CI and the controlled live acceptance path complete.

security.notes: The patch changes container base images and health-probe validation only. No secrets or production settings were modified. No claim is made that external security scanners ran.

changes: Changed all three apps/web Docker stages from node:20-alpine to node:22-alpine to match the declared node >=22 package engine and CI's Node 22 runtime.

Updated the Render keepalive workflow to parse the application health JSON and fail when success is not true or status is not healthy, including the non-healthy dependency names/statuses in the diagnostic.
evidence: Live keepalive run 40804889047 returned HTTP 200 in 42.69 seconds but its JSON payload reported status=degraded; Google Drive key path and YouTube refresh token were missing; sqlite-persistence reported healthy.
The same workflow previously considered any HTTP 200-399 response healthy without inspecting JSON readiness.
apps/web/package.json declares engines.node >=22, while the production Dockerfile previously used Node 20 in all three stages.
Repository full Vitest regression suite at CI run 39924639487 remains informational and failed 60 tests; this PR does not attempt to mask or resolve those failures.

verification.tests: CI runs are pending/retriggered by this report commit; no local execution claim.
verification.criterion: PR workflow validates the report and runs applicable repository checks; Docker runtime uses Node 22; keepalive no longer describes degraded/offline readiness as healthy.

blockedReason: This PR is a narrow hardening change only. Production readiness still requires owner-verified secrets and dispatch repository/workflow targeting, a controlled staging render with physical MP4/ffprobe verification, callback/F07 acceptance, durable storage and retrieval after a process restart, and triage of the failing informational regression suite.
